title: Rat dorsal CA1 spike times used in the ECHO listening comparison
data_provider: Yuji Ikegaya laboratory, Graduate School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, The University of Tokyo
provenance_basis: Recording methods and dataset identity confirmed by the corresponding author
study_role: Source of the neuronal stimulus in the 120-second optimized-versus-random listening comparison
recording_context: free exploration of the home cage
electrodes: Two Cambridge Neurotech ASSY-116 E-1 silicon probes
preprocessing: 300-6000 Hz band-pass filtering and common-average referencing
spike_sorting: Kilosort 2 followed by manual curation in Phy
unit_selection: Well-isolated units with trough-to-peak latency at least 0.5 ms; putative pyramidal cells, not definitive cell-type identification
animal_ethics_committee: Animal Experiment Ethics Committee of the University of Tokyo
reuse: Repurposed from a separate laboratory study; no rats were sacrificed specifically for the sonification study
data_kind: Sorted spike-time table, not raw extracellular voltage traces

columns.firing_ms: Spike time in milliseconds on the source recording clock

listening_excerpt.event_id_definition: One-based data row in spiketrain.csv, excluding the header

scope_note: The public YouTube hippocampal demonstration uses DANDI 000552 mouse data and is separate from this rat listening dataset. No other laboratory animals or participant-level survey responses are included.
